question:
A 31-year-old woman visits the clinic with complaints of heavy menstrual bleeding and lower abdominal
pain persisting for several years. The pain typically begins one week prior to the onset of menstruation.
She mentions that her mother experienced similar symptoms at the same age. On examination, she is
hemodynamically stable, with noted pallor and mild tenderness on palpation of the lower abdomen, but
no masses or organomegaly. Laboratory tests, including a complete blood cell count, urinalysis, and
urine microscopy, are normal. A transvaginal ultrasound reveals a cystic ovarian lesion with low-level
homogeneous echoes. Based on these clinical findings and investigations, which of the following
statements is accurate? Answer Choices: (A) Conservative management is preferred in most cases (B)
Laparoscopy is the not the definitive method of diagnosis (C) Imaging findings alone are sufficient for
diagnosis (D) The lesions usually appear innocuous (E) A chocolate cyst is unlikely in this case (F)
Surgical management is the mainstay of treatment (G) The cystic lesion is most likely malignant (H)
The condition is unlikely to recur after treatment (I) Hormonal therapy is the first-line treatment for all
patients (J) Pain is unrelated to the menstrual cycle in this condition
 A. Hormonal therapy is the first-line treatment for all patients
B. The lesions usually appear innocuous
C. Laparoscopy is the not the definitive method of diagnosis
D. Pain is unrelated to the menstrual cycle in this condition
E. Surgical management is the mainstay of treatment
F. The condition is unlikely to recur after treatment
G. A chocolate cyst is unlikely in this case
H. The cystic lesion is most likely malignant
I. Imaging findings alone are sufficient for diagnosis
J. Conservative management is preferred in most cases
